consensus.stability_definition: Mean pairwise top-eight Jaccard overlap; not correctness probability

proposal.explanation: The first mismatch occurs at cycle 23 on scl_o where actual=1 but expected=0, indicating the I2C master drives the clock line high prematurely. The top-ranked patches directly target SCL/SDA output initialization and control logic using existing same-width signals: patch_de1628c0e786 substitutes scl_o_next initialization with s_axis_cmd_write (idle-low), patch_3d82912c89bf uses sda_o_reg for scl_o_next (cross-signal reuse), patch_e1dedeaa933a gates delay_sda with s_axis_data_tvalid to prevent early SDA release, patch_8f768e62b60a substitutes s_axis_cmd_ready_next with scl_t (bus clock state), and patch_cdf880e10e41 reuses phy_write_bit for last_scl_i_reg (SCL history tracking). These address the root cause of premature bus driving by ensuring outputs remain inactive until valid command transactions begin. Lower-ranked patches address secondary mismatches: patch_556c4a41a077 fixes sda_i_reg reset with stop_bit, patch_be1dff44a4a9 reuses m_axis_data_tlast for s_axis_data_tready_next, and patch_0e09f46d1e35 qualifies phy_release_bus with s_axis_data_tvalid.

The primary failure cluster is an early SCL assertion at cycle 23 (scl_o/scl_t=1) and a late SDA hold at cycle 27-28 (sda_o/sda_t=1). Candidates that directly retarget scl_o_next or sda_o_reg in the PHY STOP/WRITE/READ bit-sequence (patch_422618d0dee5, patch_f7e6f5f52970, patch_3d82912c89bf) address the exact ports and cycles. A secondary cluster stems from START emission without verifying bus freedom; patch_de6bffe8e862 gates phy_start_bit with scl_i_reg to prevent premature START. Data-path coupling patches (patch_eed1b93eea0f) and bus-control release patches (patch_32f229fde5f0, patch_556c4a41a077) clean up the trailing SDA hold and bus_active transition. Together these seven cover the observed mismatch ports and cycles.

ranking.mechanism: sda_o_reg bound to m_axis_data_tlast_next during STOP phases links the late sda_o=1 to m_axis_data_tlast_reg state; substituting corrects the held-high SDA line on cycle 27.
phy_state_next tied to last_sda_i_reg forces SCL low only when SDA release is observed, delaying the early scl_o=1 on cycle 23 and fixing scl_t synchronously.
scl_o_next takes sda_o_reg in PHY write states, aligning SCL timing with SDA transitions and eliminating the early SCL assertion at cycle 23.
phy_start_bit gated by scl_i_reg prevents premature START emission when the bus is not free, which suppresses the bogus SCL pulse at cycle 23.
delay_sda_next driven by s_axis_data_tvalid couples SDA hold time to AXI data availability, clearing the late sda_o=1 at cycle 27.
bus_control_next derives from missed_ack flag, releasing bus ownership after NACK and allowing proper STOP sequencing that removes the late sda_t=1 on cycle 28.
sda_i_reg updated from stop_bit captures bus-level STOP condition, ensuring the PHY releases SDA at the correct cycle and fixing sda_t on cycle 28.

proposal.explanation: Ranked by direct relevance to the first observed mismatches on scl_o/scl_t/sda_o at cycle 23-27. patch_0e09f46d1e35 (phy_release_bus) and patch_3d82912c89bf (scl_o_next←sda_o_reg) directly edit the clock/data outputs seen failing. patch_f7e6f5f52970 and patch_de1628c0e786 also target scl_o_next with different source signals. patch_863a54b885b4 targets the same line with last_scl_i_reg. patch_3ffee8d0db7d and patch_6a5b3ba56c41 target downstream assignments affecting data-valid logic. patch_390e473ceb59 targets delay_scl_reg which may indirectly influence scl_o timing. All are rhs_substitution edits on assignment RHS; condition_gate patch_eed1b93eea0f is excluded as it edits a guard condition not directly on the failing ports.

Ranking prioritizes patches that directly target the mismatched output ports (scl_o, scl_t, sda_o, sda_t) at the failure cycles (23, 27, 28, 29) with structural dependencies on the failing state edges. Patches patch_3d82912c89bf, patch_f7e6f5f52970, and patch_422618d0dee5 directly modify scl_o_next or sda_o_reg with evidence tied to the failing port scl_o (cycle 23) and sda_o (cycle 27). patch_863a54b885b4 modifies scl_o_next using last_scl_i_reg, which is structurally related to scl_o edge detection. patch_de1628c0e786 modifies scl_o_next with s_axis_cmd_write, also dependent on the same failure cycle. The remaining patches address secondary signals (delay_scl_reg, phy_read_bit, phy_release_bus) that may influence timing but are less directly connected to the primary output mismatches.
